From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
To: Victor Madden <vmadden@brighthealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: MAP checkpoint — performance spotlight & close timeline

Victor — thanks again for the time last week. As discussed in our MAP, we ran a focused benchmarking pass against the three primary BrightHealth workloads you shared (claim-summary, triage-chat, and long-form notes). I wanted to share a compact status snapshot ahead of tomorrow's 10am PT check-in and call out clear next steps for close planning.

High-level summary (attached detailed CSV/PDF):
- Claim-summary (avg request size 320 tokens): median latency 75ms/token, 95th percentile 220ms per request, throughput ~420 reqs/s on a c5g-like baseline with continuous batching enabled.
- Triage-chat (interactive chat): median first-token latency 210ms, streaming steady-state 18 tokens/s per vGPU; good UX for 99% of sessions, occasional tail spikes tied to longer KV cache warmups.
- Long-form notes (context ~4k tokens): end-to-end completion latency averaged 3.9s for 1k-token outputs with our prefix-KV caching; throughput lower as expected (~60 reqs/s).

Observed tradeoffs and risks:
- Enabling aggressive batching gains ~30% throughput but increases first-token latency by ~30ms in interactive flows; tradeoff matters for triage-chat UX.
- Quantization profile Q4-8 gives 18% lower GPU memory and similar throughput, but we saw a small quality regression on abstractive summaries for one test prompt set (see perf_run_summaries_20270329.pdf).

Attachments: rpt_latency_throughput_20270329.csv, perf_run_summaries_20270329.pdf, map_action_tracker_20270329.xlsx

Proposed immediate actions for MAP close window:
1) Confirm target SLO for triage-chat first-token (Victor) — action: Victor to confirm whether 250ms first-token is acceptable. (owner: Victor)
2) Rishi to stage a canary with medium batching + prefix cache enabled and run 24h throughput ramp. Deliverables: canary playback logs + cost delta. (owner: rishi_malhotra)
3) Marissa to align procurement touchpoint for reserved capacity pricing estimate, target completion by Apr 6. (owner: marissa_cole)
4) Laura to prepare fallback policy that routes to lower-cost variant under sustained 99th percentile latency degradation; draft by Apr 1. (owner: laura_bennett)

Quick ask: can procurement share any hard SLA/latency thresholds that would block reserved capacity? I'll call out those constraints explicitly in the draft rollout plan.

Thanks — see you tomorrow.

--
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.inference | +1 415-555-0162

Subject: Re: MAP checkpoint — performance spotlight & close timeline

Laura — thanks for the summary and the runs. Uploaded a short CSV slice of the run where we toggled batching levels (rpt_latency_throughput_20270329.csv). Two quick notes: 

- The tail spikes Victor saw in triage-chat correlate with sessions that include a long system prompt + recent-history > 1.2k tokens; optimizing the prompt template or trimming history gives immediate reduction of 20-30% in 95th percentile.
- For the long-form workflow, adding incremental streaming (chunked generation with early-emit) reduces perceived latency even when total wall-clock completion is similar. We can demo that on the canary.

I'll spin up the canary tomorrow morning and share logs + cost delta by EOD tomorrow. Attaching a stub here: perf_run_summaries_20270329.pdf

- Rishi

Thanks Laura — useful level of detail. A couple clarifying items before tomorrow:

1) For triage-chat the stakeholder asks that 95th percentile end-to-end be <600ms when concurrent load is small (pilot-sized, ~50 concurrent). Is that achievable with medium batching + prefix cache as you propose?
2) For reserved capacity procurement: we need an estimated committed throughput to price the monthly reservation; Marissa, can you propose an initial monthly commit band so legal/procurement can draft terms?

If we can get the canary logs and the cost delta that Rishi mentioned before tomorrow, that will help our internal stakeholders short-circuit a few questions and speed signing.

Regards,
Victor
